item.title: Mixed Sizes Without Cropping

turns.text: These photos are all different shapes. Make one 10-second vertical reel, in this order. Keep each whole photo visible—don't stretch or crop them. Use a soft blurred background to fill the gaps. No music or text.

item.tests: Checks consistent vertical composition of landscape, square and portrait photos without cropping or distortion.

answer_sheet.Mixed-size handling: Fit each complete photo inside the frame without stretching or cropping. Fill unused space with a soft blurred background.
answer_sheet.Background details and transitions: Your call, as long as the background is softly blurred and each whole foreground photo stays visible.

must_haves: One silent 9:16 reel runs for approximately 10 seconds with no added text.
All five supplied photos appear in the requested order.
The landscape storefront, barista and interior photos retain their complete image boundaries.
The square latte and vertical pastries photos also remain fully visible, without cropping.
Every foreground photo retains its original proportions, with no stretching or squashing.
Unused canvas around fitted photos is filled with a soft blurred background rather than plain bars.

turns.text: These photos are all different shapes. Make one 10-second vertical 9:16 reel using all five in this order: the storefront pic, the latte pic, the pastries pic, the barista pic, and the interior pic. Keep each whole photo visible—don't stretch or crop them. Use a soft blurred background to fill the gaps. The background details and transitions are your call, as long as the background stays softly blurred and each whole foreground photo stays visible. Keep it silent, with no music or text. I'm on the free plan and don't want my credits burned, so tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t started any generation or spent any credits.** The workflow-guide check was read-only.

Your request is best handled as a **standard photo slideshow**, not AI video generation. That preserves the actual photos without cropping, stretching, or AI altering their details.

### Recommended reel
- **10 seconds, vertical 9:16**
- Five photos, about **2 seconds each**, in your exact order: storefront → latte → pastries → barista → interior
- Each original photo centered and scaled to fit completely
- An enlarged, softly blurred duplicate behind each photo fills the empty space
- Simple cuts between photos, keeping every foreground image fully visible
- No audio or added text

### Cost and cheaper options
**Using a free local editor such as Shotcut: 0 Magic Hour credits.** A 480×854 export would be a small, near-9:16 option; **360×640** is smaller and exactly 9:16. Shortening to five seconds would reduce the file size, but wouldn’t save credits over an already-free edit.

**I can’t quote a verified Magic Hour generation price here:** the connected tools don’t expose an account/pricing check or a conventional multi-photo slideshow renderer. AI generation also wouldn’t reliably preserve all five photos exactly. I wouldn’t spend your credits on that workaround.

I can provide the free-editor steps or an FFmpeg command for this exact layout, but I can’t render that conventional edit directly with the connected tools.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

turns.agent:
The cheapest option is **a local slideshow edit using 0 Magic Hour credits**. I can’t run a local editor or FFmpeg from this chat, so I can’t render or provide the finished reel here. Sorry—I should have made that limitation clearer.

To make it free in **Shotcut**:

1. Create a **360×640, 30 fps** project.
2. Put the five photos on the timeline in your requested order, **2 seconds each**.
3. Duplicate the sequence onto a video track underneath.
4. On the **bottom track**, enlarge each photo to fill the frame and apply a strong blur.
5. On the **top track**, fit each photo entirely inside the frame, preserving its proportions—no cropping or stretching.
6. Use simple cuts, add no text or audio, and export as **H.264 MP4**.

That produces the silent, 10-second vertical reel without spending any Magic Hour credits.
